_comment: Per-name classification of every DRIFTED group reported by
platform-axis name MUST appear here exactly once, classified as either
names the platform-specific fact that justifies it) or "tracked" (a
genuine unreconciled divergence; `reason` states the defect and names
the platform whose behaviour is the reference). Every entry
additionally carries a `collapsibility` object: `mechanism` (one of the
COLLAPSIBILITY_MECHANISMS) and, when mechanism is "none", a `reason`
distinct from the legitimacy `reason` above -- the two answer different
questions ("is this divergence legitimate?" vs "is this collapsible, and
by what mechanism?"). Zero unclassified entries is the bar -- this file's
entry count MUST equal the live report's drifted_count exactly.
Regenerate the name list from a fresh gate run before editing; never

_build_social_providers.reason: AWS builds Cognito-specific social identity-provider contexts for six federation types (google/facebook/amazon/apple/saml/oidc, each mapped to its own CDK UserPoolIdentityProvider* construct); Docker builds Zitadel-specific social-IdP entries for an eleven-type registry (adds github/azure/twitter/linkedin/gitlab/bitbucket) rendered as OR2 Docker secret-refs rather than CDK constructs -- two different identity backend products with different supported-provider catalogs and different secret-rendering mechanisms.

collapsibility.reason: No shared mechanism removes this: the two platforms' social-IdP catalogs are not even the same SET of provider types, so there is no single body to hoist without dropping providers one backend supports and the other does not.

_foreign_only_reason.reason: azure-vm's and docker/local's formatters build the identical 'this coordinate is native to a different platform' sentence, differing only in the embedded platform-identity phrase ('azure-vm' vs 'the docker/local self-hosted target') -- azure-vm's own module comment states it shares the identical underlying facts with local, so every one of its declared surface values matches local's exactly.

_framework_secret_def.reason: Both build the identical datrix-owned LogicalSecretDef from the same shared FRAMEWORK_JWT_KEY_PURPOSE/FRAMEWORK_JWT_KEY_AUTHORITY constants; azure's copy differs only by a cast() to satisfy a Literal type the shared constant is not typed as -- azure's own docstring states it mirrors datrix_codegen_aws's version so the Azure and AWS runtime-requirements manifests classify the same handle identically.

_generic_operator_secret_effect.reason: Both build the identical fallback sentence for an unset secret with no declared purpose, from the same logical_name parameter -- aws formats via %r, azure via an equivalent f-string single-quote literal, producing the same text for any ordinary secret name.

_resolve_identity_provider_configs.reason: AWS's package coincidentally declares this name twice for two different purposes: context.py's version only reads the pre-resolved value out of a genDSL extra_scope kwargs dict (a different function entirely), while AWSGenerator._resolve_identity_provider_configs in aws_generator.py already delegates to the shared datrix_common.identity.plan_artifact.resolve_provider_configs. Docker's docker_generator.py version independently duplicates that exact shared loader loop instead of calling it.

_resolved_flavor.reason: Both read config.platform.value off a duck-typed protocol and raise an identically-shaped GenerationError naming block_kind/block.name/service.name; azure-vm's own docstring calls it a mirror of datrix_codegen_docker's identical structural protocol -- but azure-vm's block_kind parameter is typed str (used only for error text) while docker's is typed the ManagedBlockKind enum, so the two signatures are not literally identical yet.

_supported.reason: Byte-identical bodies on azure-vm and docker/local (BlockRealization(supported=True, structural_pattern=_MANAGED_SERVICE_STRUCTURAL_PATTERN)), including the identical '*docker-compose.yml' pattern constant -- azure-vm's own module comment states this cell is reused verbatim from datrix-codegen-docker's local declaration because azure-vm self-hosts containers exactly like docker/local.

_validate_service.reason: Each platform's orchestration sequence genuinely differs in which checks run and how many: aws runs four (empty, flavor, hosting-mode, websocket-ingress); azure runs two (empty, flavor); docker runs two but conditionally, gated by an extra validate_flavors keyword aws/azure don't have. This is a per-platform check-dispatch difference, not one algorithm with cosmetic differences.

collapsibility.reason: No shared mechanism collapses a function whose whole job is choosing a different SUBSET and COUNT of checks per platform (2 vs 2-conditional vs 4) -- there is no single shared body left once the per-platform checks it dispatches to are excluded.

_widen_channel_table.reason: Both re-key a per-channel realization table at the union NotificationProvider type via the identical dict comprehension; azure-vm's own docstring states it mirrors datrix_codegen_docker.plugin.capability's own helper -- a fully generic Mapping-rekeying utility with no platform-specific logic.

build_zero_env_provisioning_context.reason: The one piece confirmed identical (per-handle secret-placeholder cardinality) is already hoisted to datrix_codegen_common.platform.zero_env.build_zero_env_secret_placeholders, which aws's copy calls. The residual bodies remain substantially different beyond that: aws returns a CDK/CloudFormation-token-based context (secrets + connections_profile + region) from a caller-supplied DerivedConnectionSurface, while azure returns a much richer Bicep/ARM-based context (connections App Configuration key-values, deploy-time ARM expressions, Key Vault stubs, managed-backend static-value overrides, RBAC role GUIDs) derived internally via its own derive_connection_surface call -- different signatures, different return shapes, different deploy-time token mechanisms.

collapsibility.reason: zero_env.py's own docstring already records that this residual piece is deliberately NOT hoisted -- the config-store seed-value emission mechanism (CDK Fn::ToJsonString vs Bicep deploymentScript heredoc) stays entirely provider-owned, since forcing it into a shared function would homogenize a genuine mechanism difference.

external_docs.reason: Both wrap the identical shared append_external_infrastructure_markdown(generator, application, files, application.hash()) call -- the entire body is already the same shared function. The only difference is each platform's own genDSL entry-point wrapper: aws takes an AWSGenerator directly, azure takes an AzureRuntimeState wrapper and additionally gates on azure_runtime.mark_once('external_docs') for its own domain-execution idempotency convention.

identity.reason: Each platform's identity() genDSL domain entry point provisions a categorically different managed identity product: AWS Cognito User Pool via CDK construct stack plus CloudFormation template; Azure Entra ID app registration plus managed identity via Bicep. This is each platform's own IdP realization, not a shared algorithm with cosmetic differences.

collapsibility.reason: No shared mechanism exists between provisioning a Cognito User Pool stack and an Entra ID app registration -- they are different products with different resource models; only the domain ENTRY POINT name is shared, not the realization.

platform_infrastructure.reason: A property accessor returning each platform's own PlatformInfrastructure singleton dataclass (AzurePlatformInfrastructure() vs DockerPlatformInfrastructure()) -- the two singletons expose the platform's own VNet/IAM/managed-service provisioning seam, which is by definition platform-specific data, not shared logic.

collapsibility.reason: The accessor body is trivial (construct-and-return); what would need collapsing is the two singleton classes' own content, which is exactly the platform-specific infrastructure contract this property exists to expose -- there is no shared body to hoist without inventing a new cross-platform infrastructure abstraction, out of this axis's scope.

provision_queue.reason: Each platform dispatches to its OWN closed RealizationDSL table for its OWN managed queue product (AWS's _AWS_QUEUE_REALIZATION_TABLE realizing SQS; Docker's _LOCAL_QUEUE_REALIZATION_TABLE realizing container/external flavors; Azure's own table realizing Service Bus) -- each is defense-in-depth for a real IaC emitter that is itself entirely platform-specific.

collapsibility.reason: The declared RealizationDSL tables are already each platform's OWN declaration surface, which is the pattern this whole design values; what remains per-platform is the queue PRODUCT itself (SQS vs Service Bus vs compose container), which has no shared mechanism to collapse into.

provision_serverless.reason: Mirrors provision_queue's shape exactly (each platform's own defense-in-depth dispatch method against its own closed table) but for the serverless block -- aws's real IaC is a materially different ServerlessStackContext/build_serverless_stack shape (a full CDK stack spec, not a resource-summary tuple), unaffected by this method.

collapsibility.reason: Same reasoning as provision_queue applied to the serverless block: the dispatch shape is already declaration-driven per platform; what remains is each platform's own serverless compute product (Lambda vs Azure Functions vs compose worker), which is the point of the per-platform declaration, not a gap to close.
